metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence — apply a “mean-reversion bias” correction: shift forecast mean toward recent 7-day average, especially if true outcome shows downward drift.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model often fails to anticipate sudden drops — add a “drop-trigger” heuristic: if true outcome drops >5% from prior day, reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3 days unless offset by event.
- Model underestimates long-term (15–30 day) mean reversion after spikes — adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average of historical prices, especially if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal from high to low (e.g., >15% drop in 3–5 days), model often fails to recognize it — apply a “reversal buffer” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days if reversal is confirmed by 2 consecutive days of decline.
